question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=1.9,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{8}, & 1\le x<5, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot 2{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{6}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =5.5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5.5-{(1.9)}^{2} \\  & =1.89.\end{aligned}
$$
